title: How a Simple Light Bulb Can Reveal Dark Matter?

scenes.text: A common LED bulb can help scientists hunt dark matter particles.
scenes.query: LED bulb dark matter detection experiment

scenes.text: Researchers coat the bulb’s glass with a thin layer of xenon, which emits faint flashes when hit by hidden particles.
scenes.label: XENON COATING
scenes.query: xenon coated light bulb dark matter detection

scenes.text: The setup uses ultra‑sensitive photomultiplier tubes to capture those rare flashes.
scenes.label: PHOTO TUBES
scenes.query: photomultiplier tubes dark matter flash detection

scenes.text: If a flash is recorded, it could indicate a weakly interacting massive particle—a leading dark matter candidate.
scenes.label: WIMP SIGNAL
scenes.query2: dark matter weakly interacting massive particle detection

scenes.text: Follow if you love learning something new.

description: A kitchen staple becomes a portal to the universe’s biggest mystery. See how scientists turn a simple bulb into a dark‑matter detector. Follow for more hidden science!
